findings.claim: Actual approved-hosted header provenance, overwrite and proxy-chain behavior remain unverified.
A deterministic short-window keyed IP bucket gives equal outputs to A and B with the same public IP, so it cannot prove independent same-NAT normal budgets.
Unforgeable server-issued tokens can separate sessions, but repeated anonymous issuance or client-key regeneration resets entitlement without another trusted admission primitive.
findings.unresolved: Owner has not defined whether one short session is the budget entitlement or budget must survive state reset.

findings.claim: Anonymous Auth changes identity lifecycle and authenticated-role access; it cannot be silently introduced solely for the limiter.
findings.compatibility: Auth-to-profile mirror and existing authenticated policies need review; no proven signup failure asserted.

findings.claim: CAPTCHA admission constrains proof issuance, but successful proofs do not demonstrate a unique client. Enterprise device signals require a material provider/privacy/access decision.
Existing Postgres can supply shared atomic budget state; new Redis is not intrinsically required. Identity/admission remains unresolved.
A new hosted metadata-probe deployment before complete CODE/INT would require an explicit sequencing exception and the full staging identity gate.
